description: Thai tax residency threshold and related mid-year/VAT filing thresholds that depend on residency-adjacent status.

rules.rule: Thai tax residency threshold (days in Thailand)
rules.conditions: Aggregate days (not necessarily consecutive) physically present in Thailand within a calendar tax year make the individual a Thai tax resident for that year.

source.label: Thai Revenue Department (EN) — Revenue Code Section 41

rules.verification_notes: Directly confirmed on RD's own English page, which states verbatim: 'Any person staying in Thailand for a period or periods aggregating 180 days or more in any tax year shall be deemed a resident of Thailand.' A genuine primary-source citation.

rules.rule: PND94 mid-year filing threshold — single / no qualifying spouse condition
rules.conditions: Jan–Jun income from Section 40(5)-40(8) qualifying types exceeding this amount triggers mid-year PND94 filing.

source.label: MBMG Group; Expat Tax Thailand (secondary, citing Revenue Code Sec. 56/56 bis)

rules.verification_notes: Consistent across two independent secondary sources. RD's own PND94 instruction PDF exists (rd.go.th/fileadmin/download/english_form/080966Ins94.pdf) but its text could not be machine-extracted during this research pass to directly quote the threshold.

rules.rule: PND94 mid-year filing threshold — married, spouse has no income
rules.conditions: Applies when married and spouse has no income; Jan–Jun qualifying income exceeding this amount triggers mid-year PND94 filing.

source.label: MBMG Group; Expat Tax Thailand (secondary, citing Revenue Code Sec. 56/56 bis)

rules.value: September 30 of the tax year (paper filing)
rules.conditions: Paper-filing deadline is solid. An e-filing extension to approximately October 8 exists but depends on a periodically-renewed Ministry of Finance notification (currently Notification No. 7, covering e-filings made 1 Feb 2024 – 31 Jan 2027) — NOT a permanent statutory rule.
rules.verification_notes: September 30 paper deadline is well corroborated. The current e-filing extension window comfortably covers the 2026 half-year filing (due ~Sept/Oct 2026). App does not currently model the e-filing extension separately — only the paper due date is stored.

rules.value: March 31 of the following year (paper filing)
rules.conditions: Standard annual PIT filing deadline for paper filing is solid law. An e-filing extension of ~8 days to early April exists historically but depends on a periodically-renewed Ministry of Finance notification, NOT permanent statute.
rules.verification_notes: IMPORTANT UNCERTAINTY FOUND: March 31 is solidly confirmed. However, the current e-filing extension notification (No. 7, dated 12 Jan 2024) only covers e-filings made through 31 January 2027. The tax-year-2026 annual return would be e-filed Feb-Apr 2027 — AFTER that cutoff. Based on the historical pattern (a prior notification, No. 3, similarly expired and was renewed as No. 7), a renewal before Feb 2027 is likely but NOT YET CONFIRMED by any notification found during this research pass. Treat the e-filing extension as 'expected based on historical pattern, unconfirmed for tax year 2026 filings' rather than settled fact. The app's stored PND90_91_DUE_DATE (2027-03-31) reflects only the solid paper deadline, which is correct either way.

rules.rule: Income types that trigger PND94 mid-year filing obligation
rules.conditions: Only these four Section 40 categories count toward the PND94 Jan-Jun threshold check — salary (40(1)) and dividend income do not.
rules.verification_notes: The app's current list matches both independent secondary sources exactly.

rules.rule: PND94: allowances are claimed at half the annual amount
rules.conditions: Personal 30,000; spouse with no income 30,000; 15,000 per child; 15,000 per parent. Deductions that depend on payments (insurance, funds, social security, donations) are the amounts actually paid in Jan–Jun; the app does not collect those, so the estimate leaves them out (higher, more cautious figure). The 65+ income exemption (up to 190,000) is applied in full, to the 40(5)-(8) income with the lowest flat-rate deduction first, since the taxpayer may choose the category.

source.label: Thai Revenue Department — Guide to Personal Income Tax Return Half Year 2023 (PND94)

rules.verification_notes: RD PND94 guide 2023, B. items 1-4 and the 'Assessable Income' note on the 190,000 exemption. OPEN: the guide's text for the 2018+ child bonus reads 'an additional 30,000 baht per child', which is the full annual bonus rather than half. The app uses half (15,000) for consistency with every other half-year amount; this gives a slightly higher provisional tax if the guide's figure is right. The RD PDF could not be read by the web fetcher; its text was extracted locally on 2026-11-25 from the RD-hosted file (English guide, tax year 2023 edition — check for a newer edition each year).

rules.rule: PND94: minimum tax on gross 40(5)-(8) income
rules.conditions: When Jan–Jun 40(5)-(8) assessable income reaches the threshold, tax payable is the greater of the net-income tax and 0.5% of that gross income (before expenses and allowances). Half-year tax is computed on half-year net income at the ordinary full-year progressive rates.

source.label: Thai Revenue Department — Guide to Personal Income Tax Return Half Year 2023 (PND94)

rules.verification_notes: RD PND94 guide 2023, C. items 8-9: 'Assessable gross income x 0.005 = tax liability'; 'your tax payable is the greater of C. item 8. or C. item 9.'; C. item 8 uses the ordinary rate table. The PND90 2024 guide additionally says the gross-income tax is ignored when it is under 5,000 baht; the PND94 guide text read does not say this, so the app does not apply the 5,000 floor to PND94 (more cautious). The RD PDF could not be read by the web fetcher; its text was extracted locally on 2026-11-25 from the RD-hosted file (English guide, tax year 2023 edition — check for a newer edition each year).

rules.rule: PND94: income level at which the 0.5% minimum tax applies
rules.conditions: Jan–Jun 40(5)-(8) assessable income of 120,000 baht or more. The guide uses both 'more than 120,000' and '120,000 baht or above'; the app uses 'or above' (more cautious).

source.label: Thai Revenue Department — Guide to Personal Income Tax Return Half Year 2023 (PND94)

rules.verification_notes: RD PND94 guide 2023, C. item 9. The RD PDF could not be read by the web fetcher; its text was extracted locally on 2026-11-25 from the RD-hosted file (English guide, tax year 2023 edition — check for a newer edition each year).

rules.rule: Annual minimum ('gross-income') tax rate on non-employment income
rules.conditions: If assessable income OTHER THAN Section 40(1) employment income is 120,000 THB or more in the tax year, tax payable is the greater of (a) the ordinary net-income tax and (b) 0.5% of that gross non-employment income before expenses and allowances — but (b) is ignored when it is under 5,000 THB. The base counts 40(2) (fees, meeting allowances, commissions), 40(3), 40(4) income included in the return (interest, dividends from Thai and foreign companies, mutual-fund profit shares), 40(5)-(8). App modelling: freelancer calculator — every Thai income entry except salary_40_1 (including 'other' and dividend entries); company-owner calculator — director fees (40(2)) plus PIT-included dividends; the 65+ exemption (up to 190,000) is taken off the base first. NOT in the base: remitted foreign income, because the app does not know its Section 40 category (this can understate the minimum for large foreign non-employment income).

source.label: Thai Revenue Department — Guide to Personal Income Tax Return 2024 (PND90), No. 11 items 8-10

rules.verification_notes: Verbatim: 'If you have assessable income other than employment income (Section 40(1)) more than 120,000 baht in the tax year ... Assessable Gross Income x 0.005 = Tax Liability'; 'your tax payable is the greater of No. 11 item 8. or No. 11 item 9.'; 'If the result is less than 5,000 baht, your tax payable is the amount in No. 11 item 8.' Read from the RD-hosted PDF; text extracted locally on 2026-11-25 because the web fetcher could not read it.

rules.rule: Annual minimum tax applies when non-employment income is at least this amount
rules.conditions: The guide says both 'more than 120,000' and '120,000 baht or above' / 'at least 120,000'; the app uses 'at least'. In practice the 5,000 THB floor (gross-income-tax-minimum-amount) means the rule only bites from 1,000,000 THB of non-employment income.

source.label: Thai Revenue Department — Guide to Personal Income Tax Return 2024 (PND90), No. 11 items 8-10

rules.verification_notes: Read from the RD-hosted PDF; text extracted locally on 2026-11-25 because the web fetcher could not read it.

rules.rule: Annual minimum tax is ignored when 0.5% of the base is below this amount
rules.conditions: 'If the result is less than 5,000 baht, your tax payable is the amount in No. 11 item 8.'

source.label: Thai Revenue Department — Guide to Personal Income Tax Return 2024 (PND90), No. 11 items 8-10
